coverage_basis: A file is locked here when a production serving entry point, scripts/10_predict_slate.py or scripts/15_price_markets.py, depends on it. slate.py and storage.py are staged into the runtime bundle by the historical contract's source_files group but were never listed in its frozen_model_source_files, so their content was shipped without being pinned. Modules that merely changed during Step 3B without being on the serving path, such as ops/refresh_current_season_state.py, are deliberately not locked here.
invariant_basis: Every divergence listed above is a serving-correctness or storage determinism fix. Two of them unblock a feed that could not be produced at all: the pricing lineage tail raised KeyError, and the live Gate 3 role path failed closed on feature names the fitted model requires. The third changes only the order rows are written in. None creates or alters a probability, price, edge, EV, line or route, none changes a training feature definition, and no fitted artifact was touched. The Step 3A adaptive architecture contract remains the authority on frozen model choices and is unchanged. The fourth and fifth divergences are the real-slate serving correction: both entry points resolved the frozen manifest against the working directory, which no checkout can satisfy, so no slate could be predicted or priced at all. They add one argument and change where the same manifest is resolved, nothing else. The current relock is the live-slate feature contract: the builder emitted none of the five competition-regime flags the fitted models require, so no slate could be scored at all once the manifest did verify. It now calls the training path's own classifier instead of producing nothing, and the classifier itself is unchanged, so no feature definition moved and no rule was restated. The current relock is the live season_progress parity correction, which is the same defect one feature along and the first one that did not announce itself: the live builder computed season_progress rather than omitting it, so nothing refused the slate and the fitted models were simply served a number they were not fit on. It now reads the classifier's own two progress columns and reproduces build_base_frame's choice between them exactly. The authority is the training definition and the training definition did not move: both src/nba_prop_quant/features.py and src/nba_prop_quant/game_context.py are byte-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests and the targeted tests both pin, and season_progress is the only column of the live slate frame whose value changed. The current relock is the T-20 capture producer, and it is the first divergence in this contract that is not on the serving path at all: this script writes the captures serving reads, and it is locked here because the historical contract byte-pins it rather than because a serving entry point imports it. The defect it corrects is that nothing ran it, so the fix is a scheduler plus the ability to ask for one offset. What it captures, how it hashes each component, how it derives capture_id and which keys the capture_run envelope carries are all unchanged and pinned syntax-tree-identical, which matters more here than elsewhere: select_capture_bundle recomputes every one of those digests before pricing may read a capture, so a change to any of them would invalidate every capture ever written rather than merely being unreviewed. The current relock is the live played-game population parity correction, which is the same class of defect as the two live-feature corrections before it and one level underneath them: not the definition of a feature but the player-game population every definition is taken over. build_base_frame keeps only the rows with minutes on them, so the fitted models' rolling priors, decay states and Kalman states are averages over appearances; BALLDONTLIE returns a row per rostered player and the live builder read that table whole, so every absence entered those averages as a zero. It refused nothing, exactly as the season_progress divergence refused nothing, and it is worse in two ways: the error has one direction, because every target is a count and the contamination can only subtract, and it is selective, because its size scales with how much of a player's recent history is absence -- so the durable players were served correct features, the absence-prone ones were marked down, and the output read as a model with a view rather than a model with a defect. The live builder now reproduces both steps build_base_frame opens with and the advanced restriction it already applies, after the leakage guard rather than before it. The authority is the training definition and the training definition did not move: src/nba_prop_quant/features.py, src/nba_prop_quant/decay.py and src/nba_prop_quant/kalman.py are byte-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests and the targeted tests both pin, and no feature definition, window, weight, threshold, marginal, copula, calibration, simulation count, Gate 3 route or fitted artifact was touched.

scripts/15_price_markets.py.divergence_reason: Combination projection fix. model_projection is the one column naming the model's central forecast for a wager and main wrote null into it for every combination prop, on the recorded ground that a combination is priced from a joint distribution over its components and that no central forecast of the combined total exists on this path. The second half of that was wrong: a distribution has a mean, this script is the stage that builds the combination's distribution at all, and ops/nba_distribution_publication.py was already publishing that mean beside the price as distribution_mean -- so the figure existed, was already published one field away, and the column a bettor reads it from said there was none, which on the public page is an empty Model Projection cell for five of the eleven prop families the model prices. main now takes the mean from whichever engine priced the row, on price_combo_lines' own branch and threshold: independent_combo_pmf's convolution of the component marginals when the frozen dependence coefficient is zero, and the mean of the very draws simulate_combo_values generates from the same correlation, draw count and seed when it is not. Both are reached by named import from nba_prop_quant.pricing, which is unchanged and byte-identical to production, so no second definition of a combination's distribution exists. Taking the mean from the engine rather than adding up the component means is a choice about which number is published and not about which is right -- a Gaussian copula couples the components' ranks and moves no mass within any component's marginal, so the sum's mean is the sum of the component means at every dependence coefficient -- but only the engine's answer is the mean of the distribution published beside it, and on rebounds_assists, the frozen policy's one dependent combination, the two differ by the simulation's own sampling error. Measured on the real served slate the targeted suite prices, every combination row's published projection equals the distribution mean the publication stage records for the same wager to 4e-15 across both branches, while the analytic sum of component means differs from the simulated engine's by up to 0.066. The priced feed carried no single column naming the model's central forecast of the player's statistic, so every consumer had to know which per-target mean applies to which prop: mu_selected_<target> for five of the six primitives, and gate3_mu_ast for assists, because the Gate 3 role state scales the selected assists mean before it reaches the marginal. main now copies that column to model_projection for every single-stat prop, and writes null for every combo prop, which is priced from a joint distribution over its components and for which no central forecast of the combined total is produced anywhere on this path. src/nba_prop_quant/slate.py.divergence_reason: Live played-game population parity fix. build_base_frame opens with df[df["minutes"].fillna(0) > 0] and then sorts by ["player_id", "date", "game_id"], so every rolling prior, decay state and Kalman state in the fitted models' feature lists -- prior_minutes10, the eleven prior_<stat>_rate10 columns, the seven decay_prior_ columns, the seven kalman_prior_ columns and the twenty-two adv_prior_ columns -- is defined as an average over a player's appearances. BALLDONTLIE's stats endpoint returns a row per rostered player, so a player who did not play arrives with zero or null minutes, and build_upcoming_slate_features was handed that table whole. Every game a player missed therefore entered his per-minute EWMs as a zero -- <stat> / minutes.clip(lower=1) is 0 / 1 on a DNP row -- and his minutes EWM as a zero, so a feature the models were fit on over appearances was served averaged over appearances and absences alike. Like the season_progress divergence this one refused nothing: every column was present, no contract objected, and the models were simply served numbers they were not fit on. Unlike it the error has a direction, because every target here is a count and the contamination can only subtract, and it is selective, because its size scales with how much of a player's recent history is absence. Measured on a twenty-round fixture in which one player misses the last four games he would have appeared in and is otherwise identical to a teammate who misses none: prior_minutes10 served 13.4438 against training's 30.0000, prior_pts_rate10 0.1793 against 0.4000, kalman_prior_min 1.0320 against 29.6999, decay_prior_min 19.8025 against 28.7124, career_games_prior 20 against 16, and days_rest 0 against 4 -- while every served feature of the teammate who missed nothing was already exact. Because mu_selected_reb and mu_selected_blk are the two ensemble targets and their decay and Kalman components are expected_minutes multiplied by a per-minute rate prior, both deflated factors enter those two multiplicatively. The live builder now takes stats through played_player_games, which reproduces both of build_base_frame's steps, and advanced through played_advanced_rows, which reproduces the inner merge on the played (game_id, player_id) keys that build_base_frame already applies to the advanced history for the reason it states in place. Both are taken after assert_slate_inputs_precede_slate rather than before it, so a same-day or later-day row cannot evade the leakage guard by being a row for a player who did not play. The authority is the training definition and the training definition did not move: src/nba_prop_quant/features.py, src/nba_prop_quant/decay.py, src/nba_prop_quant/kalman.py, src/nba_prop_quant/game_context.py, src/nba_prop_quant/model.py, src/nba_prop_quant/production.py, src/nba_prop_quant/pricing.py and src/nba_prop_quant/distributions.py are all byte-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests and the targeted tests both pin. The change is purely additive -- no line the production ref has was removed or edited, build_upcoming_slate_features is the one existing function whose body differs, its two added statements each name one of the two declared serving plumbing names, every other function in the module is syntax-tree-identical to production, and the two functions added are new. The targeted tests build the same game twice from the same historical state, once through build_base_frame and once through build_upcoming_slate_features, over histories whose absences are recent, early, and spelled with a null minutes value rather than "0:00", and require one number for every name feature_columns returns rather than for a chosen few; they also run the pre-fix builder out of Git and pin that for a history in which nobody missed a game the served frame is identical column for column, and that on a slate where one player did, no other player's row moved. This is a parity repair against already fitted models, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, mean-model routing, marginal, copula, calibration, Gate 3 route, simulation count, pricing computation or fitted artifact was changed. || Live season_progress parity fix. build_upcoming_slate_features set season_progress to a team's distinct box-score game count over a hard-coded 82. The training path takes it from classify_games' home_season_progress and visitor_season_progress -- a team's standings-counting games before the game over the season's inferred schedule length -- and build_base_frame picks between the two by is_home. season_progress is named in features.FEATURE_EXACT and therefore in the fitted models' feature lists, so the two definitions had to agree and did not: the classifier excludes the Cup Championship, the Play-In and the playoffs from its numerator and a box-score count does not, and it infers the denominator from the season rather than assuming 82. For a team forty standings games in that had also played the Cup Championship, training said 0.487805 and the live path said 0.500000, and the gap widens with every further standings-exempt game. Unlike the four divergences before it this one failed nothing: the feature was present, so no contract refused the slate and the models were served a number they were not fit on. The live builder now reads the classifier's own two progress columns, through the same classifier and the same season games table the five competition-regime flags already come from, and reproduces build_base_frame's choice exactly -- pick by is_home, fall back to (team_game_number - 1) / 82 where the classifier has no answer, clip into [0, 1]. The fallback is training's own and is reached only when a season has no inferable schedule length; the expression the row loop already computed is precisely that fallback, so it is passed through as one rather than removed. The authority is the training definition and the training definition did not move: src/nba_prop_quant/features.py and src/nba_prop_quant/game_context.py are both byte-identical to production, so no third definition exists and none was approximated. The change is purely additive -- no line the production ref has was removed or edited, build_upcoming_slate_features is the one existing function whose body differs, every other function in the module is syntax-tree-identical to production, and the two functions added are new. The targeted tests build the same game twice from the same historical state, once through build_base_frame and once through build_upcoming_slate_features, across an ordinary mid-season state and states carrying a Cup Championship, a Play-In game, playoff games and a second season, and require one number; they also run the pre-fix builder out of Git over the whole slate frame and pin that season_progress is the only column whose value moved. This is a parity repair against already fitted models, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, marginal, copula, calibration, pricing computation or fitted artifact was changed. || Live-slate feature-contract fix. build_upcoming_slate_features assembled its row dicts from scratch and emitted none of is_regular_season, is_nba_cup, is_nba_cup_championship, is_play_in or is_playoffs. All five are named in features.FEATURE_EXACT and therefore in the fitted models' feature lists, they reached the training frame only through classify_games via build_base_frame, and assert_model_feature_contract is a column-presence check with no allowance -- so every non-empty real slate was refused after the frozen manifest had verified and no slate could be predicted or priced at all. The live builder now classifies the slate with classify_games itself, which is the single definition of those five flags, rather than with a second copy of the rules; src/nba_prop_quant/game_context.py is byte-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests pin, so the answer is still only what the classifier says. The classifier is handed the season's games table as well as the slate because Play-In detection is structural: it recognises a Play-In game by a team having already completed the season's inferred schedule length, and both the inference and the count need the season's other games. Narrowing that input to the slate's seasons is exact rather than an approximation, because classify_games infers a schedule length per season and walks each season against its own counter. Nothing is defaulted: a slate whose season carries no schedule is refused rather than scored as a regular-season game. This is a parity repair against already fitted models, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, marginal, copula, calibration or fitted artifact was changed, and the change is purely additive -- no line the production ref has was removed or edited, and every function in the module except build_upcoming_slate_features is syntax-tree-identical to production. || Serving-correctness fixes only, in three parts. (1) A fail-closed historical cutoff at live slate construction: build_upcoming_slate_features now refuses box-score or advanced history that is not strictly older than the slate date, before any feature is derived and therefore before all model inference. Training consumes a shifted lagged EWM state while live inference consumes the latest historical EWM state, so the two agree only under that condition. (2) Explicit NBA slate-date semantics: America/New_York is named as the canonical slate timezone for a slate date derived from an offset-aware tip timestamp, a date-only schedule field is preserved verbatim rather than reinterpreted as UTC midnight, and a naive timestamp carrying a time of day is refused rather than guessed at. (3) Live parity for player_game_number and team_game_number, which the already fitted Gate 3 role model lists in its feature_names. Both were produced only on the historical training path, so apply_gate3_role_state failed closed on the live path and assists, points+assists and points+rebounds could not be priced. The live values reproduce the existing definitions in build_base_frame exactly and are read only from history before the slate. This is a parity repair against an already fitted model, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, or fitted artifact was changed. || Publication-context plumbing only. build_upcoming_slate_features dropped the only human-readable facts about a game that exist anywhere on this path. normalize_games already renames the schedule payload's nested home_team.abbreviation and visitor_team.abbreviation to home_team_abbreviation and visitor_team_abbreviation and already keeps its datetime, and build_upcoming_slate_features copies the games frame whole -- but it then assembled each row from a dict that kept none of the three. Every stage downstream therefore held two team integers and a date, so a published page could say who a player was playing only by inventing a team list of its own or by calling a second schedule API. The builder now carries all three forward verbatim: home_team_abbreviation, visitor_team_abbreviation, the player's own side chosen by the same is_home branch that already chooses team_id and opponent_id, and the tip timestamp as the exact string the schedule supplied, because a timestamp loses its time of day on the way to JSON. All four are None where the payload is silent, since a missing abbreviation is a fact about the schedule. No feature, prior, rolling window, leakage guard or slate-date rule was touched and no value any model is fit on changed. Purely additive: no line the production ref has was removed or edited, every function except build_upcoming_slate_features is syntax-tree-identical to production, and the added names are declared serving plumbing. Second divergence, same population one question along. Those appearance-only priors say what a player played when he played, and apply_current_injury_adjustment was reading them as what a player has to vacate: it took every OUT player's projected minutes as freed opportunity and handed the total to his team-mates. For an absence the priors were built through, that opportunity is already in them -- the rotation that actually played absorbed it, and the survivors' elevated minutes record it -- so the uplift credited the same absence twice, hardest on the teams carrying long-term injuries. The October 20 slate held the degenerate case: three OUT players had never played a game, so their minutes were the league fallback rather than any observed workload, and 55.63 minutes that had never existed were redistributed. _prior_window_participation adds the missing distinction as prior_participation_rate -- the share of a team's most recent games a player appeared in, counted over the same span and the same appearance population the minutes EWM uses -- and availability weights each OUT player's freed minutes by it. A newly absent player is unchanged at a share of one, an established absence frees nothing at a share of zero, and a partial window is prorated. OUT zeroing, the elasticity allocation, the 42-minute cap and the usage multiplier are untouched, the addition states no threshold or weight of its own, and no probability, price, edge, EV, quantile, line or routing computation was reached.

src/nba_prop_quant/storage.py.divergence_reason: Operational storage determinism only. upsert_parquet concatenated and deduplicated without a final sort, so the stored row order of mutable rolling state depended on the arrival order of the incoming batch and two runs over the same semantic records produced different files. Rows are now ordered by the dataset's declared key columns with a stable sort and pinned NaN placement, and the index is reset before the write. The sort runs after deduplication so keep-last still resolves a replaced record in favour of the incoming batch. No value is computed, altered or rounded: this changes the order bytes are written in, nothing else.
